jasper: FYI the nightly perf trace is missing kernel timelines — nsys shows CUPTI load errors inside the inference container.

anita: Can you paste the nsys command and the error you see?

jasper: Ran: `nsys profile --output /tmp/run -t cupti,cublas,cuda --trace-fork-before-exec true --sample=none -- ./run_inference.sh`
Error snippet:
```
nsys: Warning: could not load CUPTI library '/usr/local/cuda/extras/CUPTI/lib64/libcupti.so': No such file or directory
nsys: CUPTI-based timing disabled, kernel timeline will be incomplete
```

maria: That usually means the container doesn't have the CUDA extras mounted. Which driver + cuda/toolkit are on the host?

jasper: Host driver 525.60, container has CUDA 11.8 from the base image, nsight-systems 2023.3 shipped in our profiling image. We saw a perf regression in the nightly: runtime started picking the "fallback_gemm" kernel in production traces (latency +8%). The missing CUPTI means our kernel-selection heuristics can't see actual runtimes.

sam: Two quick checks: `ldd /usr/local/cuda/extras/CUPTI/lib64/libcupti.so` inside the container (if present) and `ls -l /usr/local/cuda/extras/CUPTI/`. Also try running the container with `-v /usr/local/cuda/extras/CUPTI:/usr/local/cuda/extras/CUPTI:ro`.

jasper: ldd output (inside repro container after mounting):
```
$ ldd /usr/local/cuda/extras/CUPTI/lib64/libcupti.so
	linux-vdso.so.1 =>  (0x00007ffc3d5c9000)
	libcuda.so.1 => /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 (0x00007f3a2c8b4000)
	libc.so.6 => /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libc.so.6 (0x00007f3a2c4f7000)
```
No missing deps after mount. But when we don't mount, nsys still logs the same missing-CUPTI message.

maria: If the host driver is older than the toolkit's expected driver, CUPTI might be incompatible. For 11.8 we usually want driver >= 520.x. 525 should be OK but nsight + container combos can be picky. Also container runtime needs the nvidia-container-toolkit to make `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1` visible.

anita: This is interesting because our kernel-selection falls back to safe kernels when timeline sampling is unavailable. That explains the regression: without CUPTI telemetry the heuristic reduces batch-size aggressiveness and picks conservative GEMM kernels. We need to either restore CUPTI or expose a synthetic profiling signal.

sam: Workarounds: (1) Mount CUPTI from host into the profiling image (quick). (2) Upgrade host driver to 535.x and match nsight release (longer). (3) As a short-term software mitigation, set env `REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNELS=optimized_gemm,optimized_matmul` when running the batching perf tests to bypass the heuristic.

infra-bot: Job #ci/prof-nightly reported: trace-collector failed to capture cupti. Follow-up: https://ci.redwood.example/1234 (automated) :robot_face:

anita: Action items: jasper - repro with mounted CUPTI and post full nsys log; maria - check cluster node driver versions and nvidia-container-toolkit config; sam - draft small runtime toggle PR to opt-out of heuristic when CUPTI missing.

jasper: Reproduced locally by running container with `-v /usr/local/cuda/extras/CUPTI:/usr/local/cuda/extras/CUPTI:ro` — nsys now shows kernel timelines and the runtime picks the fast GEMM kernel again. I'll upload the trimmed profile to GCS and link in the PR. Thanks :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Uploaded profile to gs://redwood-profiles/nightly/1790012345_profile.qdrep

jasper: Posting repro steps here so others can try quickly:
```
docker run --gpus all -it --rm \
  -v /usr/local/cuda/extras/CUPTI:/usr/local/cuda/extras/CUPTI:ro \
  -v /var/run/nvidia-container-runtime:/var/run/nvidia-container-runtime:ro \
  profiling-image:2023.3 \
  bash -lc "nsys profile --output /tmp/run -t cupti,cublas,cuda --sample=none -- ./run_inference.sh"
```
If you see `could not load CUPTI` without the mount, try the mount or install the CUDA extras into the image.

anita: Perfect. Once PR to force kernels is up we'll toggle the heuristic in CI so nightlies don't regress while infra schedules driver/image fixes. :rocket:
